label: conj:root-of-unity-mtc-truncation
title: At $q = e^{2\pi i / k}$, the KLR algebra truncates to a Modular Tensor Category of non-abelian anyons
html:
Conjecture (root-of-unity MTC truncation). Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of the anyonic substrate. Fix k \geq 2. Specialise the deformation parameter at a primitive k-th root of unity on the unit circle:

  q \;=\; e^{2\pi i / k} \;\in\; S^1.

The cyclotomic quotient of the KLR algebra realising H_n(R, q) becomes finite-dimensional. The infinite Kashiwara crystal \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) truncates to a finite component supported on partitions with at most k - 1 columns. The category of cyclotomic-KLR modules is a Modular Tensor Category \mathrm{MTC}_k [bakalovkirillov2001]. The simple objects of \mathrm{MTC}_k are non-abelian anyons [kitaev2006, nayak2008]. Their fusion rules match the truncated crystal's Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. Their braiding is the action of B_n on H_n(R, q) specialised at q = e^{2\pi i / k}.

Algorithmic role. Switching the substrate parameter to a primitive k-th root of unity converts the open-ended Hecke evaluation into a finite-rank fusion calculation. The engine enumerates the truncated crystal nodes and reads the F- and R-matrices of \mathrm{MTC}_k directly from the \sigma_{s_i} generators evaluated at the chosen root.

Conjectural status. The Bakalov–Kirillov MTC structure on cyclotomic-KLR modules at a root of unity is established [bakalovkirillov2001, khovanovlauda2009]. The truncation of the Kashiwara crystal at roots of unity is also established [kashiwara1991]. We conjecture the identification of the simple \mathrm{MTC}_k objects with the substrate's non-abelian anyon spectrum at the chosen k. To falsify this, exhibit a QOU particle at q = e^{2\pi i / k} whose fusion does not match the predicted \mathrm{MTC}_k rule.
heading: Conjecture
